input.quote: (ii) Either Party may, without consent of the other Party, assign this Agreement in whole to (i) in the case of RevMed, its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in the case of a Change of Control or (ii) in the case of Sanofi, its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Section 15.2 already gives Sanofi the two carve-outs we require: assignment to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610) and assignment to a successor in a sale of substantially all relevant assets, merger or acquisition without consent (p0611). RevMed has no termination right on a Sanofi Change of Control (RevMed's grounds are exhaustively material breach, insolvency, Sanofi Competing Product and cessation, per Section 12.3(c)); Sanofi's own right to terminate on a RevMed Change of Control (Section 12.2(a)(ii)) benefits us and is not flagged. The gap is on the Vendor side: Section 15.2(a)(ii) lets RevMed assign the entire Agreement to its Change of Control successor with no Sanofi consent at all, and nothing prevents RevMed (or its acquirer) from being or becoming a Sanofi competitor. We target the preferred position rather than the fallback because the fallback's "other assignments require consent" would strip Sanofi's no-consent Affiliate right, which we will not give up. The redline conditions RevMed's Change of Control assignment on Sanofi's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and adds an express bar on assignment to a Sanofi competitor, leaving Sanofi's prong and the Acquiror Family conditions untouched.

proposal.summary: Condition RevMed's Change of Control assignment on Sanofi's consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bar assignment to a Sanofi competitor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We are comfortable with Sanofi's affiliate and M&A assignment rights, but our position is that RevMed may not assign without our consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor of Sanofi. We have therefore split Section 15.2(a)(ii) so RevMed's Change of Control assignment is consent-gated and added an express competitor bar; Sanofi's prong is unchanged.

ops.newText: Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement in whole to its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction, and RevMed may, with the consent of Sanofi (not to be unreasonably withheld), assign this Agreement in whole to its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in the case of a Change of Control. In no event shall RevMed assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder to a competitor of Sanofi.
